structure.title: Act I · A street fight and a party
structure.text: The servants can get a brawl going before the heads of either family arrive. Romeo slips into the enemy household for an entirely different girl. The two lovers have spoken and kissed before they learn the names that make their meeting dangerous.

structure.title: Acts II–III · Two calendars
structure.text: A secret marriage can be arranged in remarkable haste. It cannot erase the obligations of friends who meet on a hot street. The audience knows the new family relationship while some of the people prepared to fight know nothing of it.

structure.title: Acts IV–V · When messages travel slowly
structure.text: The Capulets begin arranging Juliet's future at home. Adults and lovers devise plans that depend on somebody being in the right place with the right information. Hours and minutes acquire the force that family names had at the start.

people.name: Juliet and the Nurse
people.role: Daughter and the woman who raised her
people.text: The Nurse remembers Juliet's first steps. Juliet can entrust her with errands she could never ask her mother to undertake. Their affection is secure long before it becomes clear whether their ideas of a tolerable marriage agree.

people.name: Mercutio and Tybalt
people.role: Men quick to take a challenge
people.text: Mercutio is Romeo's friend. Tybalt is Juliet's cousin. A mockery of cowardice or an insult to a family can acquire an audience for whom backing down would itself require explanation.

context.title: The prologue gives away the ending
context.text: The chorus tells the audience where the lovers' story leads. Suspense shifts onto all the occasions when somebody could have done something else. An apparently minor delay can be almost unbearable to watch.

notice.text: How do they talk together at the party?
notice.why: Their first conversation makes a sonnet between two speakers. Juliet takes up Romeo's religious imagery and finds things she can do with it. The attraction has a sound before it has a history.

passages.quote: palm to palm is holy palmers’ kiss

notice.text: Listen for people giving the time.
notice.why: Juliet waiting for the Nurse can make a few hours sound endless. Once the adults start moving dates forward, the young people's impatience and their elders' haste become dangerous in combination.

opening: Romeo goes to a party expecting to pine for one woman and meets another who changes everything. Juliet discovers that the stranger she wants belongs to the family she has been taught to hate. Their attraction is quick, funny, and mutual; the difficulty is finding somewhere it can exist. Around them, young men defend their honour with swords and parents make plans without asking. Shakespeare makes first love feel expansive enough to contain a whole future, inside a city determined to narrow it.
